To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the threshold voltages of n- and P-MOSFET devices increase with increasing X-ray dose levels, the propagation delay time of the inverter increases with increasing X-ray doses, the voltage transfer characteristic of the inverter shifts to higher voltage levels with increasing X-ray radiation doses, the performance of an inverting chain, a three-stage ring oscillator and a 4 × 4 shift register decreases with increasing radiation dose level.
1.5keV X-rays cause degradation in the electrical characteristics of CMOS devices and circuits.
1.5 KeV X-ray radiation causes a shift of the threshold voltage of MOSFETs and a degradation of the performance of the logic circuits.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiation effects on MOS devices and circuits.
the total dose radiation effects of 1. 5 keV X-rays on CMOS devices.
the total dose radiation effects on CMOs devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
1.5 KeV X-rays do cause degradation in the performance of MOS devices.
the 1.5keV X-ray radiation has a detrimental effect on the performance of the CMOS devices and circuits.
the threshold voltage of both n- and p-type MOSFETs decreases with radiation dose.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the threshold voltage of the n-MOSFET increased and that of the p-MOSFETS decreased with increasing radiation dose, and the propagation delay time of the inverter increased.
the radiation effects are more pronounced on p-MOSFETS than on n-MOSFET.
the radiation effects are not significant for these devices at the dose level of 10 7 rads(Si) and the device characteristics degrade only slightly with increasing radiation dose level.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1.5-keV X-rays are a viable alternative for testing the total dose response of devices and circuits.
the threshold voltages of both n- and p-channel devices increase after irradiation.
the 1.5keV X-ray radiation can be used as a tool to study the total dose radiation effects on CMOs devices.
